newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil strike begins, mixed turnout.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil strike begins, mixed turnout.

text.p: An eight-hour strike by two main Venezuelan oil workers' unions began at 0500 local time/0900 GMT this morning, but there were conflicting reports of its success.

A senior union leader said preliminary reports suggested it was a "total success", but an oil company spokesman said the stoppage attracted only 11 percent support among union members in one major refinery.
Carlos Ortega, president of the Fedepetrol union, told Reuters, "The stoppage is going ahead normally... we are receiving information from the regions indicating that it is a total success."

But Danny Romero, public relations manager of the 305,000 barrel per day (bpd) Cardon refinery, said there was 89 percent turnout by union workers and that operations were completely normal. Cardon is operated by Maraven, a subsidiary of state oil company PDVSA.
"We have had 89 percent attendance in the refinery and operations are not affected in the slightest. Products are leaving the plant normally and we are running at full capacity," Romero said.
PDVSA said previously that if the strike went ahead it would maintain output using non-union workers.
Ortega said he had received no reaction from PDVSA regarding the unions' demands on Friday morning, but PDVSA issued a notice to workers on Thursday saying the strike was unjustified.
The unions Fedepetrol and Fetrahidrocarburos are campaigning for more performance-related pay, more money for contract workers and more inflation-related pay rises.
